summary: Settings step 4: a project can override four Chat & agents settings (follow-up while the agent works, where new chats run, the runtime mode new chats start in, file diff cards). The list lives in src/shared/project-settings.ts (SCOPABLE_SETTINGS); each override is one settings row keyed project:<pathKey>:<settingKey>, pathKey being the worktree manager's normalised path, and resolves as project override ?? global ?? default through one pure effectiveSetting. The backend serves settings:project-overrides / -override-set / -override-remove and answers settings:get(key, projectPath) with the effective value; START_SESSION resolves the machine runtime mode for the chat's project (a worktree chat's parent). Desktop: a Scope combobox on Chat & agents (All projects, Recent, by workspace, override counts), Overridden marker and Reset per row, non-scopable rows disabled with a reason, a new Runtime mode row, search results showing effective values, and a Projects list with launch config and override counts and Open. The phone and Android read the runtime-mode default for the project they start a session in. Unknown setting keys in override rows are logged and ignored, never deleted.

automated: npm test (vitest: scopable list, resolution order, pathKey junction and Windows case variant, unknown-key tolerance, device-auth gating of override keys, backend and renderer consumers, and the first new chat in a project with a cold renderer cache)

notExercised: Android: the Kotlin change (getSetting with a project path, NewSessionCoordinator reading the project's runtime mode) was not compiled or run here; no JDK was available on this machine. CI's Android job covers it.
The phone was not driven on a device; the client change is covered by the jest api test.

Older backends ignore the extra settings:get argument and answer with the machine value, and have no override channels, so Settings on a desktop pointed at one shows no overrides; not exercised against a real older server.

In multi-machine mode the renderer's override cache reads the base backend, so a remote machine's project shows the base backend's overrides in Settings while that machine's own START_SESSION uses its own DB.
